arguments.command:
python3 << 'EOF'
import math

# National Defense expenditures (in millions of dollars) for fiscal years 1933-1941
expenditures = {
    1933: 680,
    1934: 531,
    1935: 689,
    1936: 900,
    1937: 929,
    1938: 1029,
    1939: 1206,
    1940: 1657,
    1941: 6301  # Includes emergency ship construction from March 1941
}

# Calculate year-to-year log growth rates
years = list(range(1934, 1942))  # 1934-1941
log_growth_rates = []

for year in years:
    prev_year = year - 1
    growth_rate = math.log(expenditures[year] / expenditures[prev_year])
    log_growth_rates.append(growth_rate)
    print(f"{year}: ln({expenditures[year]}/{expenditures[prev_year]}) = ln({expenditures[year]/expenditures[prev_year]:.4f}) = {growth_rate:.6f}")

print("\n--- Log growth rates ---")
print(log_growth_rates)

# Calculate mean (using population mean, not sample mean)
n = len(log_growth_rates)
mean = sum(log_growth_rates) / n
print(f"\nMean: {mean:.6f}")

# Calculate population standard deviation
# Using population std dev (N, not N-1)
variance = sum((x - mean) ** 2 for x in log_growth_rates) / n
pop_std = math.sqrt(variance)
print(f"Population standard deviation: {pop_std:.6f}")

# Coefficient of variation = std dev / mean
# Using absolute value of mean since we're measuring volatility
cv = pop_std / abs(mean)
print(f"\nCoefficient of Variation: {cv:.6f}")
print(f"Rounded to nearest hundredth: {cv:.2f}")
EOF
